findings: Large well-defined hepatocellular carcinoma in the right hepatic lobe with heterogeneous but largely hyperechoic echotexture. Color Doppler demonstrates intralesional arteries.

findings: Ultrasound of the right lobe shows peripheral ill defined HCC (horizontal arrow) with thrombus of the right posterior portal venous branch (other two arrows). Gray-scale image shows thrombus within portal vein. Doppler images show larger than normal arterial branch
column3: which is due to hypervascular HCC in the periphery (siphon effect) and secondary to portal venous thrombus (arterial buffer response).

findings: Ultrasound shows a mixed hyperechoic and hypoechoic HCC in a cirrhotic liver. A mass with mixed echogenicity in a cirrhotic liver is typical
column3: but not specific for HCC. The round echogenic component of the mass has no correlation to any alterations on the CT and MR of this case.

findings: Gray-scale ultrasound shows a well-defined round isoechoic mass in the left lobe with peripheral hypoechoic components. Contrast enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) shows homogeneous hypervascularity except for peripheral portions
column3: which enhance at different arterial time points. Note washout on late venous phase
column4: classic for HCC. Poor hemodynamics of the hepatic parenchyma result in poor portal venous phase liver enhancement. Courtesy Dr. Stephanie J. Wilson
